105:## Tunnel WireGuard pour le jumpbox (Mac)
106-
107-Le LAN de provisioning (`10.10.10.0/24`) est volontairement isolé - un
108-MacBook posé sur le réseau domestique (côté WAN de l'Opal) n'a par défaut
109-aucun chemin vers les hosts. Pour piloter Ansible/Terraform/kubectl depuis
110-ce Mac sans être physiquement/en Wi-Fi sur le LAN de l'Opal, un tunnel
111-WireGuard (`wg_mgmt`) tourne côté Opal :
112-
113-- Interface serveur `wg_mgmt` sur `10.10.11.1/24`, port UDP `51821` (choisi
114-  pour ne pas entrer en conflit avec la fonctionnalité "WireGuard Server"
115-  native de GL.iNet - `/etc/config/wireguard_server`, port `51820` -
116-  présente sur ce firmware mais désactivée/non utilisée ; on n'y touche pas).
117-- Un peer pour le Mac (`10.10.11.2/32`), avec `route_allowed_ips=1`.
118-- Une zone firewall `wg_mgmt` + forwarding `wg_mgmt -> lan` (sans quoi le
119-  tunnel se connecte mais ne route rien vers `10.10.10.0/24`) + une règle
120-  WAN autorisant `udp/51821` en entrée.
121-
122-### Prérequis découverts en le mettant en place
123-
124-- **Dropbear sur ce firmware n'a pas de support Ed25519** (build embarqué,
125-  `strings /usr/sbin/dropbear` ne contient aucune référence ed25519) - la
126-  clé `~/.ssh/id_ed25519_homelab` utilisée pour les hosts Rocky ne
127-  fonctionnera PAS pour SSH vers l'Opal, même une fois ajoutée à
128-  `/etc/dropbear/authorized_keys` (échoue silencieusement côté client :
129-  `Offering public key... / Authentications that can continue: publickey,password`
130-  sans autre indice). Il faut une clé **RSA** dédiée, ex. :
131-  ```bash
132-  ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 -f ~/.ssh/id_rsa_opal -C "opal-admin@jumpbox"
133-  # une fois la clé publique ajoutée à /etc/dropbear/authorized_keys sur l'Opal :
134-  ssh -o HostKeyAlgorithms=+ssh-rsa -o PubkeyAcceptedAlgorithms=+ssh-rsa \
135-    -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa_opal root@10.10.10.1
136-  ```
137-- `wireguard-tools`/`kmod-wireguard` sont déjà installés sur l'Opal (servent
138-  normalement à sa propre fonction client VPN voyage - `gl-sdk4-wg-client`,
139-  policy routing `policy_default_rt_vpn*` - non touchée par ce qui suit).
140-
141-### Mise en place
142-
143-```bash
144-# Cote Mac : générer sa propre paire de clés (la clé privée ne quitte jamais
145-# la machine, jamais commit - voir .gitignore : *.key)
146-mkdir -p ~/.wireguard-homelab && chmod 700 ~/.wireguard-homelab
147-wg genkey | tee ~/.wireguard-homelab/mac-jumpbox.key | wg pubkey \
148-  > ~/.wireguard-homelab/mac-jumpbox.pub
149-
150-# Pousse la config sur l'Opal (backup UCI auto + génère la paire de clés
151-# côté Opal si absente + reload network/firewall)
152-./router/deploy-wireguard.sh 10.10.10.1 "$(cat ~/.wireguard-homelab/mac-jumpbox.pub)"
153-```
154-
155-Le script affiche la clé publique de l'Opal à la fin - à coller dans le
156-`Peer.PublicKey` du fichier client ci-dessous.
157-
158-Fichier client (`~/.wireguard-homelab/mac-jumpbox.conf`, `chmod 600`) :
159-
160-```ini
161-[Interface]
162-PrivateKey = REDACTED de ~/.wireguard-homelab/mac-jumpbox.key>
163-Address = 10.10.11.2/24
164-
165-[Peer]
166-PublicKey = <clé publique affichée par deploy-wireguard.sh>
167-Endpoint = <IP de l'Opal côté réseau domestique>:51821
168-AllowedIPs = 10.10.10.0/24, 10.10.11.0/24
169-PersistentKeepalive = 25
170-```
171-
172-```bash
173-sudo wg-quick up ~/.wireguard-homelab/mac-jumpbox.conf
174-# ... travail sur le homelab ...
175-sudo wg-quick down ~/.wireguard-homelab/mac-jumpbox.conf
176-```
177-
178-**⚠️ L'IP `Endpoint` est l'adresse DHCP de l'Opal côté réseau domestique
179-(`ip -br a` sur l'Opal, interface `eth0.2` - observée à `192.168.2.109` au
180-moment de la mise en place) - elle peut changer à chaque renouvellement de
181-bail DHCP. Fixer une réservation DHCP statique pour la MAC de l'Opal
182-(`94:83:c4:60:84:c0`) sur le routeur domestique pour que ça ne casse pas
183-plus tard - ce n'est pas gérable depuis ce repo, c'est côté routeur
184-domestique.**
185-
186:## Tailscale (accès depuis n'importe où, sans dépendre du tunnel WireGuard)
187-
188:Le tunnel WireGuard ci-dessus ne fonctionne que depuis le réseau domestique (le Mac doit pouvoir joindre
189-le WAN de l'Opal). Pour un accès depuis n'importe où sans dépendre de ça, `host1` fait office de "subnet
190-router" Tailscale pour `10.10.10.0/24` - annoncé via `ansible/roles/tailscale/` (playbook dédié
191-`ansible/playbooks/tailscale.yml`, groupe `tailscale_router` dans l'inventaire), gardé séparé de
192-`bootstrap.yml`.
193-
194-**Pourquoi `host1` et pas l'Opal directement** : l'Opal tourne sur un SoC Siflower SF19A28 avec seulement
195-128 Mo de RAM/flash (target OpenWrt `siflower-1806`, cf. plus haut) - support Tailscale incertain sur ce
196-matériel. `host1` (Rocky Linux 9, x86_64, 32 Go RAM) a un paquet RPM officiel et zéro contrainte.
197-
198-### Mise en place (déjà faite, pour référence)
199-
200-```bash
201-cd ansible
202-ansible-playbook -i inventory/hosts.yml playbooks/tailscale.yml
203-```
204-
205-Puis, une fois (interactif - `tailscale up` a besoin d'une authentification navigateur ou d'une authkey,
206-volontairement non automatisé pour ne pas stocker de credential dans ce repo) :
207-
208-```bash
209-ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_homelab foo@10.10.10.10 "sudo tailscale up --advertise-routes=10.10.10.0/24 --hostname=host1-homelab"
210-```
211-
212-Ouvrir l'URL affichée pour autoriser la machine sur le tailnet. **Étape facilement manquée** : la route
213-`10.10.10.0/24` doit ensuite être approuvée manuellement dans la console web -
214-https://login.tailscale.com/admin/machines → `host1-homelab` → *Subnet routes* → activer
215-`10.10.10.0/24`. Sans ça, la machine apparaît "Connected" et se ping via son IP Tailscale, mais rien
216-derrière (`10.10.10.x`) n'est routé - symptôme trompeur, ressemble à un problème réseau alors que c'est
217-juste une route non approuvée.
218-
219-### Piège rencontré : VPN commercial en conflit
220-
221-Un VPN commercial actif en parallèle (NordVPN dans ce cas) empêche la route de sous-réseau de fonctionner
222-même une fois approuvée - son kill switch / sa propre table de routage par défaut entre en concurrence
223-avec la route Tailscale vers `10.10.10.0/24`. Si `ping 10.10.10.10` échoue alors que le device apparaît
224-bien "Connected" dans Tailscale et que la route est approuvée, désactiver tout autre client VPN sur la
225-machine avant de chercher plus loin.
226-
227-WireGuard (`wg_mgmt`) reste en place en parallèle comme filet de secours, pas remplacé.
228-
229-## Mise à jour de WireGuard sur l'Opal
230-
231-Deux voies concrètes :
232-
233-1. **Firmware officiel** : GL.iNet publie régulièrement des mises à jour
234-   pour le SFT1200 (dl.gl-inet.com/router/sft1200) incluant des correctifs
235-   liés à WireGuard - à vérifier/appliquer en premier, c'est le chemin le
236-   plus simple.
237-2. **SDK GL.iNet** (github.com/gl-inet/sdk) : le SFT1200/SF1200 utilise la
238-   target `siflower-1806`. Ça permet de recompiler `wireguard-tools` /
239-   `kmod-wireguard` contre le kernel exact de l'Opal et d'installer le
240-   `.ipk` résultant via `opkg` - un `opkg upgrade` simple ne suffit pas ici
241-   car le module kernel doit matcher l'ABI du kernel en place.
242-
243-À noter : le protocole WireGuard lui-même n'a pas eu de rupture de
244-compatibilité depuis sa sortie - un module plus ancien reste tout à fait
245-interopérable avec des pairs récents. Mettre à jour apporte surtout des
246-correctifs de sécurité et des améliorations d'outillage, pas de la
247-connectivité en plus.

132-  ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 -f ~/.ssh/id_rsa_opal -C "opal-admin@jumpbox"
133-  # une fois la clé publique ajoutée à /etc/dropbear/authorized_keys sur l'Opal :
134-  ssh -o HostKeyAlgorithms=+ssh-rsa -o PubkeyAcceptedAlgorithms=+ssh-rsa \
135-    -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa_opal root@10.10.10.1
136-  ```
137-- `wireguard-tools`/`kmod-wireguard` sont déjà installés sur l'Opal (servent
138-  normalement à sa propre fonction client VPN voyage - `gl-sdk4-wg-client`,
139-  policy routing `policy_default_rt_vpn*` - non touchée par ce qui suit).
140-
141-### Mise en place
142-
143-```bash
144-# Cote Mac : générer sa propre paire de clés (la clé privée ne quitte jamais
145-# la machine, jamais commit - voir .gitignore : *.key)
146-mkdir -p ~/.wireguard-homelab && chmod 700 ~/.wireguard-homelab
147-wg genkey | tee ~/.wireguard-homelab/mac-jumpbox.key | wg pubkey \
148-  > ~/.wireguard-homelab/mac-jumpbox.pub
149-
150-# Pousse la config sur l'Opal (backup UCI auto + génère la paire de clés
151-# côté Opal si absente + reload network/firewall)
152-./router/deploy-wireguard.sh 10.10.10.1 "$(cat ~/.wireguard-homelab/mac-jumpbox.pub)"
153-```
154-
155-Le script affiche la clé publique de l'Opal à la fin - à coller dans le
156-`Peer.PublicKey` du fichier client ci-dessous.
157-
158-Fichier client (`~/.wireguard-homelab/mac-jumpbox.conf`, `chmod 600`) :
159-
160-```ini
161-[Interface]
162-PrivateKey = REDACTED de ~/.wireguard-homelab/mac-jumpbox.key>
163-Address = 10.10.11.2/24
164-
165-[Peer]
166-PublicKey = <clé publique affichée par deploy-wireguard.sh>
167-Endpoint = <IP de l'Opal côté réseau domestique>:51821
168-AllowedIPs = 10.10.10.0/24, 10.10.11.0/24
169-PersistentKeepalive = 25
170-```
171-
172-```bash
173-sudo wg-quick up ~/.wireguard-homelab/mac-jumpbox.conf
174-# ... travail sur le homelab ...
175-sudo wg-quick down ~/.wireguard-homelab/mac-jumpbox.conf
176-```
177-
178-**⚠️ L'IP `Endpoint` est l'adresse DHCP de l'Opal côté réseau domestique
179-(`ip -br a` sur l'Opal, interface `eth0.2` - observée à `192.168.2.109` au
180-moment de la mise en place) - elle peut changer à chaque renouvellement de
181-bail DHCP. Fixer une réservation DHCP statique pour la MAC de l'Opal
182-(`94:83:c4:60:84:c0`) sur le routeur domestique pour que ça ne casse pas
183-plus tard - ce n'est pas gérable depuis ce repo, c'est côté routeur
184-domestique.**
185-
186:## Tailscale (accès depuis n'importe où, sans dépendre du tunnel WireGuard)
187-
188:Le tunnel WireGuard ci-dessus ne fonctionne que depuis le réseau domestique (le Mac doit pouvoir joindre
189-le WAN de l'Opal). Pour un accès depuis n'importe où sans dépendre de ça, `host1` fait office de "subnet
190-router" Tailscale pour `10.10.10.0/24` - annoncé via `ansible/roles/tailscale/` (playbook dédié
191-`ansible/playbooks/tailscale.yml`, groupe `tailscale_router` dans l'inventaire), gardé séparé de
192-`bootstrap.yml`.
193-
194-**Pourquoi `host1` et pas l'Opal directement** : l'Opal tourne sur un SoC Siflower SF19A28 avec seulement
195-128 Mo de RAM/flash (target OpenWrt `siflower-1806`, cf. plus haut) - support Tailscale incertain sur ce
196-matériel. `host1` (Rocky Linux 9, x86_64, 32 Go RAM) a un paquet RPM officiel et zéro contrainte.
197-
198-### Mise en place (déjà faite, pour référence)
199-
200-```bash
201-cd ansible
202-ansible-playbook -i inventory/hosts.yml playbooks/tailscale.yml
203-```
204-
205-Puis, une fois (interactif - `tailscale up` a besoin d'une authentification navigateur ou d'une authkey,
206-volontairement non automatisé pour ne pas stocker de credential dans ce repo) :
207-
208-```bash
209-ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_homelab foo@10.10.10.10 "sudo tailscale up --advertise-routes=10.10.10.0/24 --hostname=host1-homelab"
210-```
211-
212-Ouvrir l'URL affichée pour autoriser la machine sur le tailnet. **Étape facilement manquée** : la route
213-`10.10.10.0/24` doit ensuite être approuvée manuellement dans la console web -
214-https://login.tailscale.com/admin/machines → `host1-homelab` → *Subnet routes* → activer
215-`10.10.10.0/24`. Sans ça, la machine apparaît "Connected" et se ping via son IP Tailscale, mais rien
216-derrière (`10.10.10.x`) n'est routé - symptôme trompeur, ressemble à un problème réseau alors que c'est
217-juste une route non approuvée.
218-
219-### Piège rencontré : VPN commercial en conflit
220-
221-Un VPN commercial actif en parallèle (NordVPN dans ce cas) empêche la route de sous-réseau de fonctionner
222-même une fois approuvée - son kill switch / sa propre table de routage par défaut entre en concurrence
223-avec la route Tailscale vers `10.10.10.0/24`. Si `ping 10.10.10.10` échoue alors que le device apparaît
224-bien "Connected" dans Tailscale et que la route est approuvée, désactiver tout autre client VPN sur la
225-machine avant de chercher plus loin.
226-
227-WireGuard (`wg_mgmt`) reste en place en parallèle comme filet de secours, pas remplacé.
228-
229-## Mise à jour de WireGuard sur l'Opal
230-
231-Deux voies concrètes :
232-
233-1. **Firmware officiel** : GL.iNet publie régulièrement des mises à jour
234-   pour le SFT1200 (dl.gl-inet.com/router/sft1200) incluant des correctifs
235-   liés à WireGuard - à vérifier/appliquer en premier, c'est le chemin le
236-   plus simple.
237-2. **SDK GL.iNet** (github.com/gl-inet/sdk) : le SFT1200/SF1200 utilise la
238-   target `siflower-1806`. Ça permet de recompiler `wireguard-tools` /
239-   `kmod-wireguard` contre le kernel exact de l'Opal et d'installer le
240-   `.ipk` résultant via `opkg` - un `opkg upgrade` simple ne suffit pas ici
241-   car le module kernel doit matcher l'ABI du kernel en place.
242-
243-À noter : le protocole WireGuard lui-même n'a pas eu de rupture de
244-compatibilité depuis sa sortie - un module plus ancien reste tout à fait
245-interopérable avec des pairs récents. Mettre à jour apporte surtout des
246-correctifs de sécurité et des améliorations d'outillage, pas de la
247-connectivité en plus.

content.text:
You don't need WireGuard for this. Your Mac is already connected straight to the homelab network: it has the address 10.10.10.240 on Wi-Fi and its router is the Opal (10.10.10.1). That's the best setup for the migration, because nothing sits between you and the nodes. My earlier advice to use WireGuard was wrong for your setup.

The rule that matters for migration day is not to reach the cluster through Tailscale. Tailscale runs on host1, and host1 gets reset and rebooted during the migration, so you'd lose your connection partway through.

**If you're ever on your home Wi-Fi instead**, the tunnel is already set up from August. The config file is at `~/.wireguard-homelab/mac-jumpbox.conf`.
```sh
sudo wg-quick up ~/.wireguard-homelab/mac-jumpbox.conf     # connect
ping 10.10.10.10                                          # check it works
sudo wg-quick down ~/.wireguard-homelab/mac-jumpbox.conf   # when done
```
- **The tunnel's address may be out of date.** The config points at `192.168.2.109:51821`, which is the address the Opal had on your home network in August. Your home router can hand the Opal a new address, and if it has, the tunnel won't connect. To fix that, look up the Opal's current address in your home router, change the `Endpoint` line, and ideally reserve that address for the Opal's MAC `94:83:c4:60:84:c0`.
- **Turn off other VPNs first.** Disconnect Tailscale (and any other VPN, such as NordVPN) before you bring the tunnel up, or they'll fight over the 10.10.10.x addresses.

Before starting the migration, just check you're still on the Opal's Wi-Fi with `route -n get 10.10.10.10`. It should show `interface: en0` and no `gateway`. I'll do that check as part of Phase 0.

=== .github/workflows/deploy.yml
name: Deploy

# Rolling/release pipeline — manually triggered.
# Requires the self-hosted runner registered on the jumpbox (needs the
# WireGuard tunnel up to reach the hosts/cluster on 10.10.10.0/24 - see
# bare-metal/README.md, "Tunnel WireGuard pour le jumpbox").
# See docs/ci-cd.md for runner setup instructions.
# After Terraform and Ansible complete, ArgoCD is already watching the git repo
# and will roll out any manifest changes automatically. This job waits for that
# sync to confirm the cluster is fully converged before marking the run green.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      target:
        description: "What to deploy"
        required: true
        default: all
        type: choice
        options:
          - terraform
          - ansible
          - all
      ansible_tags:
        description: "Ansible tags (e.g. containerd, kubeadm) — blank = full playbook"
        required: false
        default: ""
      dry_run:
        description: "Dry-run (plan/check only, no changes applied)"
        required: false
        default: "false"
        type: choice
        options:
          - "false"
          - "true"

jobs:
  terraform-apply:
    name: Terraform apply
    runs-on: [self-hosted, homelab]
    if: inputs.target == 'terraform' || inputs.target == 'all'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: "~1.9"

      - name: Init
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/cluster-bootstrap init

      - name: Plan
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/cluster-bootstrap plan -no-color -out=tfplan

      - name: Apply
        if: inputs.dry_run == 'false'
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/cluster-bootstrap apply -auto-approve tfplan

  ansible-run:
    name: Ansible playbook
    runs-on: [self-hosted, homelab]
    needs: [terraform-apply]
    if: |
      always() &&
      !cancelled() &&
      (inputs.target == 'ansible' || inputs.target == 'all') &&
      (needs.terraform-apply.result == 'success' || needs.terraform-apply.result == 'skipped')
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Run playbook
        run: |
          CMD="ansible-playbook -i ansible/inventory/hosts.yml ansible/playbooks/bootstrap.yml"
          if [ -n "${{ inputs.ansible_tags }}" ]; then
            CMD="$CMD --tags ${{ inputs.ansible_tags }}"
          fi
          if [ "${{ inputs.dry_run }}" = "true" ]; then
            CMD="$CMD --check --diff"
          fi
          $CMD
        env:
          ANSIBLE_FORCE_COLOR: "1"

  argocd-verify:
    name: Verify ArgoCD sync
    runs-on: [self-hosted, homelab]
    needs: [terraform-apply, ansible-run]
    if: |
      always() &&
      !cancelled() &&
      inputs.dry_run == 'false' &&
      (needs.ansible-run.result == 'success' || needs.ansible-run.result == 'skipped') &&
      (needs.terraform-apply.result == 'success' || needs.terraform-apply.result == 'skipped')
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Wait for ArgoCD to sync all apps
        run: |
          export KUBECONFIG="$(pwd)/clusters/homelab/kubeconfig"
          echo "Waiting up to 5 minutes for all ArgoCD apps to sync..."
          timeout 300 bash -c '
            until kubectl -n argocd get applications -o json \
              | jq -e "[.items[] | .status.sync.status] | length > 0 and all(. == \"Synced\")" \
              > /dev/null 2>&1; do
              echo "  still waiting... ($(kubectl -n argocd get applications --no-headers 2>/dev/null | awk "{print \$2}" | sort | uniq -c | tr -s " " | sed "s/^ //"))"
              sleep 15
            done
          '
          echo "All apps synced. Checking health..."
          kubectl -n argocd get applications

      - name: Assert all apps healthy
        run: |
          export KUBECONFIG="$(pwd)/clusters/homelab/kubeconfig"
          UNHEALTHY=$(kubectl -n argocd get applications -o json \
            | jq -r '.items[] | select(.status.health.status != "Healthy") | .metadata.name')
          if [ -n "$UNHEALTHY" ]; then
            echo "Unhealthy apps: $UNHEALTHY"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "All apps are Synced and Healthy."
=== .github/workflows/plan.yml
name: Plan

# Terraform plan and Ansible dry-run on PRs and main pushes.
# Requires the self-hosted runner registered on the jumpbox (needs the
# WireGuard tunnel up to reach the hosts/cluster on 10.10.10.0/24 - see
# bare-metal/README.md, "Tunnel WireGuard pour le jumpbox").
# See docs/ci-cd.md for runner setup instructions.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "terraform/**"
      - "ansible/**"
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "terraform/**"
      - "ansible/**"

jobs:
  terraform-plan:
    name: Terraform plan
    runs-on: [self-hosted, homelab]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: "~1.9"
          terraform_wrapper: true

      - name: Init
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/cluster-bootstrap init

      - name: Plan
        id: plan
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/cluster-bootstrap plan -no-color -out=tfplan
        continue-on-error: true

      - name: Comment plan on PR
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const plan = `${{ steps.plan.outputs.stdout }}`;
            const status = '${{ steps.plan.outcome }}' === 'success' ? '✅' : '❌';
            const body = `#### Terraform Plan ${status}
            <details><summary>Show plan</summary>

            \`\`\`hcl
            ${plan.slice(0, 60000)}
            \`\`\`

            </details>
            *Pushed by @${{ github.actor }}, action: \`${{ github.event_name }}\`*`;

            const { data: comments } = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
            });
            const existing = comments.find(c =>
              c.user.type === 'Bot' && c.body.includes('Terraform Plan')
            );
            if (existing) {
              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                comment_id: existing.id,
                body,
              });
            } else {
              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: context.issue.number,
                body,
              });
            }

      - name: Fail if plan failed
        if: steps.plan.outcome == 'failure'
        run: exit 1

      - name: Upload plan artifact
        if: steps.plan.outcome == 'success'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: tfplan-${{ github.sha }}
          path: terraform/cluster-bootstrap/tfplan
          retention-days: 1

  ansible-check:
    name: Ansible dry-run
    runs-on: [self-hosted, homelab]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Check mode (no changes applied)
        run: |
          ansible-playbook \
            -i ansible/inventory/hosts.yml \
            ansible/playbooks/bootstrap.yml \
            --check --diff
        env:
          ANSIBLE_FORCE_COLOR: "1"

name: Validate

# Runs on every push and PR — no cluster access required.
# Catches format, syntax, and lint errors before they reach main.

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  terraform:
    name: Terraform fmt & validate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: "~1.9"

      - name: Format check
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/cluster-bootstrap fmt -check -recursive

      - name: Init (no backend)
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/cluster-bootstrap init -backend=false

      - name: Validate
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/cluster-bootstrap validate

  ansible:
    name: Ansible lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install tools
        run: pip install ansible-core==2.17.* ansible-lint==24.*

      # ansible-core ships only ansible.builtin; the roles also use
      # ansible.posix.sysctl and community.general.modprobe.
      - name: Install collections
        run: ansible-galaxy collection install -r ansible/requirements.yml

      - name: Lint
        run: ansible-lint ansible/
        env:
          ANSIBLE_ROLES_PATH: ansible/roles

  yaml:
    name: YAML lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - run: pip install yamllint

      - run: yamllint -c .yamllint.yml clusters/ ansible/ apps/

name: Deploy

# Rolling/release pipeline — manually triggered.
# Requires the self-hosted runner registered on the jumpbox (needs the
# WireGuard tunnel up to reach the hosts/cluster on 10.10.10.0/24 - see
# bare-metal/README.md, "Tunnel WireGuard pour le jumpbox").
# See docs/ci-cd.md for runner setup instructions.
# After Terraform and Ansible complete, ArgoCD is already watching the git repo
# and will roll out any manifest changes automatically. This job waits for that
# sync to confirm the cluster is fully converged before marking the run green.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      target:
        description: "What to deploy"
        required: true
        default: all
        type: choice
        options:
          - terraform
          - ansible
          - all
      ansible_tags:
        description: "Ansible tags (e.g. containerd, kubeadm) — blank = full playbook"
        required: false
        default: ""
      dry_run:
        description: "Dry-run (plan/check only, no changes applied)"
        required: false
        default: "false"
        type: choice
        options:
          - "false"
          - "true"

jobs:
  terraform-apply:
    name: Terraform apply
    runs-on: [self-hosted, homelab]
    if: inputs.target == 'terraform' || inputs.target == 'all'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: "~1.9"

      - name: Init
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/cluster-bootstrap init

      - name: Plan
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/cluster-bootstrap plan -no-color -out=tfplan

      - name: Apply
        if: inputs.dry_run == 'false'
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/cluster-bootstrap apply -auto-approve tfplan

  ansible-run:
    name: Ansible playbook
    runs-on: [self-hosted, homelab]
    needs: [terraform-apply]
    if: |
      always() &&
      !cancelled() &&
      (inputs.target == 'ansible' || inputs.target == 'all') &&
      (needs.terraform-apply.result == 'success' || needs.terraform-apply.result == 'skipped')
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Run playbook
        run: |
          CMD="ansible-playbook -i ansible/inventory/hosts.yml ansible/playbooks/bootstrap.yml"
          if [ -n "${{ inputs.ansible_tags }}" ]; then
            CMD="$CMD --tags ${{ inputs.ansible_tags }}"
          fi
          if [ "${{ inputs.dry_run }}" = "true" ]; then
            CMD="$CMD --check --diff"
          fi
          $CMD
        env:
          ANSIBLE_FORCE_COLOR: "1"

  argocd-verify:
    name: Verify ArgoCD sync
    runs-on: [self-hosted, homelab]
    needs: [terraform-apply, ansible-run]
    if: |
      always() &&
      !cancelled() &&
      inputs.dry_run == 'false' &&
      (needs.ansible-run.result == 'success' || needs.ansible-run.result == 'skipped') &&
      (needs.terraform-apply.result == 'success' || needs.terraform-apply.result == 'skipped')
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Wait for ArgoCD to sync all apps
        run: |
          export KUBECONFIG="$(pwd)/clusters/homelab/kubeconfig"
          echo "Waiting up to 5 minutes for all ArgoCD apps to sync..."
          timeout 300 bash -c '
            until kubectl -n argocd get applications -o json \
              | jq -e "[.items[] | .status.sync.status] | length > 0 and all(. == \"Synced\")" \
              > /dev/null 2>&1; do
              echo "  still waiting... ($(kubectl -n argocd get applications --no-headers 2>/dev/null | awk "{print \$2}" | sort | uniq -c | tr -s " " | sed "s/^ //"))"
              sleep 15
            done
          '
          echo "All apps synced. Checking health..."
          kubectl -n argocd get applications

      - name: Assert all apps healthy
        run: |
          export KUBECONFIG="$(pwd)/clusters/homelab/kubeconfig"
          UNHEALTHY=$(kubectl -n argocd get applications -o json \
            | jq -r '.items[] | select(.status.health.status != "Healthy") | .metadata.name')
          if [ -n "$UNHEALTHY" ]; then
            echo "Unhealthy apps: $UNHEALTHY"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "All apps are Synced and Healthy."

name: Plan

# Terraform plan and Ansible dry-run on PRs and main pushes.
# Requires the self-hosted runner registered on the jumpbox (needs the
# WireGuard tunnel up to reach the hosts/cluster on 10.10.10.0/24 - see
# bare-metal/README.md, "Tunnel WireGuard pour le jumpbox").
# See docs/ci-cd.md for runner setup instructions.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "terraform/**"
      - "ansible/**"
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "terraform/**"
      - "ansible/**"

jobs:
  terraform-plan:
    name: Terraform plan
    runs-on: [self-hosted, homelab]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: "~1.9"
          terraform_wrapper: true

      - name: Init
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/cluster-bootstrap init

      - name: Plan
        id: plan
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/cluster-bootstrap plan -no-color -out=tfplan
        continue-on-error: true

      - name: Comment plan on PR
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const plan = `${{ steps.plan.outputs.stdout }}`;
            const status = '${{ steps.plan.outcome }}' === 'success' ? '✅' : '❌';
            const body = `#### Terraform Plan ${status}
            <details><summary>Show plan</summary>

            \`\`\`hcl
            ${plan.slice(0, 60000)}
            \`\`\`

            </details>
            *Pushed by @${{ github.actor }}, action: \`${{ github.event_name }}\`*`;

            const { data: comments } = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
            });
            const existing = comments.find(c =>
              c.user.type === 'Bot' && c.body.includes('Terraform Plan')
            );
            if (existing) {
              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                comment_id: existing.id,
                body,
              });
            } else {
              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: context.issue.number,
                body,
              });
            }

      - name: Fail if plan failed
        if: steps.plan.outcome == 'failure'
        run: exit 1

      - name: Upload plan artifact
        if: steps.plan.outcome == 'success'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: tfplan-${{ github.sha }}
          path: terraform/cluster-bootstrap/tfplan
          retention-days: 1

  ansible-check:
    name: Ansible dry-run
    runs-on: [self-hosted, homelab]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Check mode (no changes applied)
        run: |
          ansible-playbook \
            -i ansible/inventory/hosts.yml \
            ansible/playbooks/bootstrap.yml \
            --check --diff
        env:
          ANSIBLE_FORCE_COLOR: "1"

name: Validate

# Runs on every push and PR — no cluster access required.
# Catches format, syntax, and lint errors before they reach main.

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  terraform:
    name: Terraform fmt & validate

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

        with:
          terraform_version: "~1.9"

      - name: Init (no backend)

      - name: Validate

  ansible:
    name: Ansible lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:

      - name: Install tools

      - name: Install collections

content.text:
A GitHub runner can do this, but the runner has to live **on your Mac**, and it's riskier than running the migration directly with me. If you want it, here's what's needed.

## Where the runner runs

The runner has to be your Mac. Your existing `deploy.yml` and `plan.yml` already assume this, and nothing else works:
- **host1, host2 and host3 are all reset and rebooted in Phase 2**, so a runner on any of them would die mid-job.
- **The Opal can't run it**: it has 128 MB and isn't a CPU GitHub's runner supports.
- **GitHub's cloud runners can't reach 10.10.10.0/24**, your private network.

Register the runner on the Mac as a service, labelled `homelab`. Get a token on the repo's Settings → Actions → Runners → New self-hosted runner page, or from `gh api -X POST repos/maximepatry/k8s-homelab/actions/runners/registration-token -q .token`, then:
```sh
./config.sh --url https://github.com/maximepatry/k8s-homelab --token <TOKEN> --labels homelab
./svc.sh install && ./svc.sh start
```
Installed this way it runs as your user, so it can use your existing `~/.ssh` keys, kubeconfig and the CA backup. None of these need to go into GitHub secrets, and the CA key shouldn't.

## ⚠️ Fix this before registering it

**Your repo is public, and `plan.yml` runs on `pull_request`.** Once a runner exists, anyone who forks the repo and opens a pull request can run their own code on your Mac. That code would have your SSH keys to every node and admin access to the cluster. Before registering, do both:
1. In Settings → Actions → General, require approval for workflows from **all outside collaborators**.
2. In `plan.yml`, either drop the `pull_request` trigger or add `if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository` to its jobs.

## The migration workflow

It would be a new `migrate-control-plane.yml`, started by hand, with **one job per runbook phase**. Each job would require your approval through a GitHub environment, so the run stops between phases until you click Approve. A few things would break if done naively:
- **It has to reach `main` first, in its own PR.** GitHub only lists hand-started workflows that are on the default branch, and PR #3 can't be merged early.
- **Phase 3 merges PR #3 from inside the run.** The job needs `contents: write` and `pull-requests: write` permissions.
- **Phases 4 and later need to check out `main` explicitly.** `actions/checkout` defaults to the commit the run started from, which is before the merge, so Ansible and Terraform would quietly deploy the old config and point Cilium back at host1.
- **The runbook's judgment checks become hard assertions.** For example: host3's USB network card came back on .30, every node has the right internal IP, and the CA secret is restored before ArgoCD installs cert-manager.
- **The Mac must stay awake and on the Opal's Wi-Fi.** Run `caffeinate` during the migration: if the Mac sleeps, the job dies partway through a phase.
- **Your existing `deploy.yml` has bugs on a Mac runner.** It calls `timeout`, which macOS doesn't have (`brew install coreutils` provides it as `gtimeout`). It also reads the kubeconfig from `clusters/homelab/kubeconfig` inside the checkout, but that file isn't in git, so the step would fail.

## My recommendation

For this **one-time migration that wipes the cluster**, run it directly with me. When a phase does something unexpected, a person can look and adapt, and a workflow can only fail. The workflow is also about an hour of extra work and gets used once.

The runner is still worth setting up afterwards for `deploy.yml` and `plan.yml`, once the security fixes and the Mac bugs above are done.

I can open a PR with the security fix and the `deploy.yml` fixes now, and write the phased migration workflow too if you'd still rather go that way.

content.content:
# CI/CD

Three GitHub Actions workflows (`.github/workflows/`):

| Workflow | Trigger | Runs on | What it does |
|----------|---------|---------|---------------|
| `validate.yml` | every push/PR | `ubuntu-latest` (hosted) | `terraform fmt`/`validate` (no backend, no cluster access needed), `ansible-lint`, `yamllint` |
| `plan.yml` | PR/push touching `terraform/**` or `ansible/**` | `[self-hosted, homelab]` | `terraform plan` against the real cluster, `ansible-playbook --check --diff` |
| `deploy.yml` | manual (`workflow_dispatch`) | `[self-hosted, homelab]` | `terraform apply`, `ansible-playbook`, waits for ArgoCD to sync/heal |

`validate.yml` needs no LAN access (hosted runner is fine). `plan.yml` and `deploy.yml` need to actually
reach the hosts and the cluster API (`10.10.10.0/24`), so they require a **self-hosted runner** — there's
no GitHub-hosted alternative for a private homelab network.

## Self-hosted runner setup (on the jumpbox)

The runner needs to run somewhere with a path into `10.10.10.0/24` — that's the Mac jumpbox, over the
WireGuard tunnel from `bare-metal/README.md` ("Tunnel WireGuard pour le jumpbox"). Bring the tunnel up
before the runner needs to reach anything (it does not manage the tunnel itself).

1. On GitHub: repo → **Settings → Actions → Runners → New self-hosted runner**, pick macOS/ARM64. Copy the
   `./config.sh --url ... --token ...` command it gives you (the token is single-use, generated per
   registration — don't reuse an old one from these docs).
2. On the Mac:
   ```bash
   mkdir -p ~/actions-runner && cd ~/actions-runner
   # paste the download + config.sh commands from step 1
   ```
3. When prompted for labels, add `homelab` (the workflows target `[self-hosted, homelab]` specifically —
   the default `self-hosted` label alone isn't enough).
4. Run it as a background service so it survives reboots/logout:
   ```bash
   ./svc.sh install
   ./svc.sh start
   ```
5. Make sure the runner's environment has what the jobs need on `PATH`: `terraform`, `ansible-playbook`,
   `ansible-lint`, `kubectl`, `jq`. The runner inherits whatever shell environment it was installed under
   — if you installed these via Homebrew under your normal user, a launchd-managed service may not pick up
   `/opt/homebrew/bin` unless it's on the system `PATH`; verify with a workflow run rather than assuming.

## Kubeconfig on the runner

`terraform/cluster-bootstrap`'s providers and `deploy.yml`'s `argocd-verify` job both read
`clusters/homelab/kubeconfig` from the runner's own checkout (workspace-relative, not `~/.kube/config`) —
it's produced once by `ansible-playbook playbooks/bootstrap.yml` (the control-plane role fetches it) and
persists on the runner's disk across workflow runs, since the self-hosted runner isn't ephemeral like a
GitHub-hosted one. The very first `plan.yml`/`deploy.yml` run before any manual bootstrap has happened will
fail for lack of this file — that's expected, not a bug; run the initial bootstrap by hand once (see
`docs/ansible.md`, `docs/terraform.md`) before relying on the pipeline for it.

variable "kubeconfig_path" {
  description = "Path to the admin kubeconfig fetched by the Ansible control-plane role"
  type        = string
  default     = "../../clusters/homelab/kubeconfig"
}

variable "repo_url" {
  description = "Git repo ArgoCD syncs from"
  type        = string
  default     = "https://github.com/maximepatry/k8s-homelab"
}

variable "target_revision" {
  description = "Branch ArgoCD tracks for all root Applications"
  type        = string
  default     = "main"
}

variable "argocd_chart_version" {
  description = "argo-cd Helm chart version (argoproj Helm repo)"
  type        = string
  default     = "7.7.*"
}
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.5"

  required_providers {
    kubernetes = {
      source  = "hashicorp/kubernetes"
      version = "~> 2.31"
    }
    helm = {
      source  = "hashicorp/helm"
      version = "~> 2.14"
    }
    kubectl = {
      source  = "alekc/kubectl"
      version = "~> 2.0"
    }
  }
}

provider "kubernetes" {
  config_path = var.kubeconfig_path
}

provider "helm" {
  kubernetes {
    config_path = var.kubeconfig_path
  }

name: Plan

# Terraform plan and Ansible dry-run on PRs and main pushes.
# Runs on the self-hosted runner on the Mac jumpbox (must be on the Opal LAN
# or have the WireGuard tunnel up to reach 10.10.10.0/24 - see
# bare-metal/README.md, "Tunnel WireGuard pour le jumpbox").
# See docs/ci-cd.md for runner setup and the required runner .env.
#
# SECURITY: this repo is public and the runner holds SSH keys + cluster-admin
# credentials. Jobs only run for pushes and for PRs whose head branch lives in
# this repo - a PR from a fork never reaches the self-hosted runner.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "terraform/**"
      - "ansible/**"
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "terraform/**"
      - "ansible/**"

permissions:
  contents: read

# Never run a plan/check concurrently with a deploy against the same cluster.
concurrency:
  group: homelab-cluster
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  terraform-plan:
    name: Terraform plan
    if: github.event_name == 'push' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: [self-hosted, homelab]
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Check runner environment
        run: |
          : "${HOMELAB_TFSTATE:?HOMELAB_TFSTATE not set - see docs/ci-cd.md (runner .env)}"
          : "${HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG:?HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG not set - see docs/ci-cd.md (runner .env)}"
          test -f "$HOMELAB_TFSTATE"
          test -f "$HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG"
          echo "TF_VAR_kubeconfig_path=$HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: "~1.9"
          terraform_wrapper: true

      # State is local and lives in the operator's checkout; point this
      # checkout at the same file instead of planning against an empty state.
      - name: Init
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/cluster-bootstrap init -input=false -backend-config="path=$HOMELAB_TFSTATE"

      - name: Plan
        id: plan
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/cluster-bootstrap plan -input=false -lock-timeout=5m -no-color
        continue-on-error: true

      - name: Comment plan on PR
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        env:
          # Passed via env, not interpolated into the script, so plan output
          # can't inject JavaScript.
          PLAN: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.stdout }}
          OUTCOME: ${{ steps.plan.outcome }}
        with:
          script: |
            const plan = process.env.PLAN || '';
            const status = process.env.OUTCOME === 'success' ? '✅' : '❌';
            const body = [
              `#### Terraform Plan ${status}`,
              '<details><summary>Show plan</summary>',
              '',
              '```hcl',
              plan.slice(0, 60000),
              '```',
              '',
              '</details>',
              `*Pushed by ${context.actor}, action: \`${context.eventName}\`*`,
            ].join('\n');

            const { data: comments } = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
            });
            const existing = comments.find(c =>
              c.user.type === 'Bot' && c.body.includes('Terraform Plan')
            );
            if (existing) {
              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                comment_id: existing.id,
                body,
              });
            } else {
              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: context.issue.number,
                body,
              });
            }

      - name: Fail if plan failed
        if: steps.plan.outcome == 'failure'
        run: exit 1

  ansible-check:
    name: Ansible dry-run
    if: github.event_name == 'push' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: [self-hosted, homelab]
    defaults:
      run:
        # Run from ansible/ so ansible/ansible.cfg (become, SSH key, roles
        # path) is picked up - it's only read from the current directory.
        working-directory: ansible
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # The control-plane role writes the kubeconfig into the checkout; seed
      # it with the live one so check mode compares against reality.
      - name: Seed kubeconfig
        run: |
          : "${HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG:?HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG not set - see docs/ci-cd.md (runner .env)}"
          install -m 600 "$HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG" ../clusters/homelab/kubeconfig

      - name: Check mode (no changes applied)
        run: ansible-playbook playbooks/bootstrap.yml --check --diff
        env:
          ANSIBLE_FORCE_COLOR: "1"

name: Deploy

# Rolling/release pipeline - manually triggered.
# Runs on the self-hosted runner on the Mac jumpbox (must be on the Opal LAN
# or have the WireGuard tunnel up to reach 10.10.10.0/24 - see
# bare-metal/README.md, "Tunnel WireGuard pour le jumpbox").
# See docs/ci-cd.md for runner setup and the required runner .env.
# After Terraform and Ansible complete, ArgoCD is already watching the git repo
# and will roll out any manifest changes automatically. This job waits for that
# sync to confirm the cluster is fully converged before marking the run green.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      target:
        description: "What to deploy"
        required: true
        default: all
        type: choice
        options:
          - terraform
          - ansible
          - all
      ansible_tags:
        description: "Ansible tags (e.g. containerd, kubeadm) - blank = full playbook"
        required: false
        default: ""
      dry_run:
        description: "Dry-run (plan/check only, no changes applied)"
        required: false
        default: "false"
        type: choice
        options:
          - "false"
          - "true"

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: homelab-cluster
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  terraform-apply:
    name: Terraform apply
    runs-on: [self-hosted, homelab]
    if: inputs.target == 'terraform' || inputs.target == 'all'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Check runner environment
        run: |
          : "${HOMELAB_TFSTATE:?HOMELAB_TFSTATE not set - see docs/ci-cd.md (runner .env)}"
          : "${HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG:?HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG not set - see docs/ci-cd.md (runner .env)}"
          test -f "$HOMELAB_TFSTATE"
          test -f "$HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG"
          echo "TF_VAR_kubeconfig_path=$HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: "~1.9"

      # State is local and lives in the operator's checkout; share that file.
      - name: Init
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/cluster-bootstrap init -input=false -backend-config="path=$HOMELAB_TFSTATE"

      - name: Plan
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/cluster-bootstrap plan -input=false -lock-timeout=5m -no-color -out=tfplan

      - name: Apply
        if: inputs.dry_run == 'false'
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/cluster-bootstrap apply -input=false -lock-timeout=5m -auto-approve tfplan

  ansible-run:
    name: Ansible playbook
    runs-on: [self-hosted, homelab]
    needs: [terraform-apply]
    if: |
      always() &&
      !cancelled() &&
      (inputs.target == 'ansible' || inputs.target == 'all') &&
      (needs.terraform-apply.result == 'success' || needs.terraform-apply.result == 'skipped')
    defaults:
      run:
        # ansible/ansible.cfg is only read from the current directory.
        working-directory: ansible
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Seed kubeconfig
        run: |
          : "${HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG:?HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG not set - see docs/ci-cd.md (runner .env)}"
          install -m 600 "$HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG" ../clusters/homelab/kubeconfig

      - name: Run playbook
        env:
          ANSIBLE_FORCE_COLOR: "1"
          # Inputs via env, never interpolated into the shell script.
          TAGS: ${{ inputs.ansible_tags }}
          DRY_RUN: ${{ inputs.dry_run }}
        run: |
          args=(playbooks/bootstrap.yml)
          if [ -n "$TAGS" ]; then args+=(--tags "$TAGS"); fi
          if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "true" ]; then args+=(--check --diff); fi
          ansible-playbook "${args[@]}"

      # If the playbook (re)wrote the kubeconfig (e.g. after a rebuild), copy
      # it back so the operator's checkout and later runs use the new one.
      - name: Sync kubeconfig back
        if: inputs.dry_run == 'false'
        run: |
          if ! cmp -s ../clusters/homelab/kubeconfig "$HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG"; then
            install -m 600 ../clusters/homelab/kubeconfig "$HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG"
            echo "kubeconfig updated at $HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG"
          fi

  argocd-verify:
    name: Verify ArgoCD sync
    runs-on: [self-hosted, homelab]
    needs: [terraform-apply, ansible-run]
    if: |
      always() &&
      !cancelled() &&
      inputs.dry_run == 'false' &&
      (needs.ansible-run.result == 'success' || needs.ansible-run.result == 'skipped') &&
      (needs.terraform-apply.result == 'success' || needs.terraform-apply.result == 'skipped')
    steps:
      - name: Wait for ArgoCD to sync all apps
        run: |
          export KUBECONFIG="${HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG:?HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG not set - see docs/ci-cd.md}"
          echo "Waiting up to 5 minutes for all ArgoCD apps to sync..."
          # Plain deadline loop: macOS (the runner) has no `timeout`.
          deadline=$((SECONDS + 300))
          until kubectl -n argocd get applications -o json \
            | jq -e '[.items[] | .status.sync.status] | length > 0 and all(. == "Synced")' \
            > /dev/null 2>&1; do
            if [ "$SECONDS" -ge "$deadline" ]; then
              echo "Timed out waiting for ArgoCD sync"
              kubectl -n argocd get applications
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "  still waiting... ($(kubectl -n argocd get applications --no-headers 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $2}' | sort | uniq -c | tr -s ' ' | sed 's/^ //'))"
            sleep 15
          done
          echo "All apps synced. Checking health..."
          kubectl -n argocd get applications

      - name: Assert all apps healthy
        run: |
          export KUBECONFIG="$HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG"
          UNHEALTHY=$(kubectl -n argocd get applications -o json \
            | jq -r '.items[] | select(.status.health.status != "Healthy") | .metadata.name')
          if [ -n "$UNHEALTHY" ]; then
            echo "Unhealthy apps: $UNHEALTHY"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "All apps are Synced and Healthy."

        run: |
          export KUBECONFIG="$HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG"
          UNHEALTHY=$(kubectl -n argocd get applications -o json \
            | jq -r '.items[] | select(.status.health.status != "Healthy") | .metadata.name')
          if [ -n "$UNHEALTHY" ]; then

            exit 1
          fi

name: Deploy

# Rolling/release pipeline — manually triggered.
# Requires the self-hosted runner registered on the jumpbox (needs the
# WireGuard tunnel up to reach the hosts/cluster on 10.10.10.0/24 - see
# bare-metal/README.md, "Tunnel WireGuard pour le jumpbox").
# See docs/ci-cd.md for runner setup instructions.
# After Terraform and Ansible complete, ArgoCD is already watching the git repo
# and will roll out any manifest changes automatically. This job waits for that
# sync to confirm the cluster is fully converged before marking the run green.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      target:
        description: "What to deploy"
        required: true
        default: all
        type: choice
        options:
          - terraform
          - ansible
          - all
      ansible_tags:
        description: "Ansible tags (e.g. containerd, kubeadm) — blank = full playbook"
        required: false
        default: ""
      dry_run:
        description: "Dry-run (plan/check only, no changes applied)"
        required: false
        default: "false"
        type: choice
        options:
          - "false"
          - "true"

jobs:
  terraform-apply:
    name: Terraform apply
    runs-on: [self-hosted, homelab]
    if: inputs.target == 'terraform' || inputs.target == 'all'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: "~1.9"

      - name: Init
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/cluster-bootstrap init

      - name: Plan
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/cluster-bootstrap plan -no-color -out=tfplan

      - name: Apply
        if: inputs.dry_run == 'false'
        run: terraform -chdir=terraform/cluster-bootstrap apply -auto-approve tfplan

  ansible-run:
    name: Ansible playbook
    runs-on: [self-hosted, homelab]
    needs: [terraform-apply]
    if: |
      always() &&
      !cancelled() &&
      (inputs.target == 'ansible' || inputs.target == 'all') &&
      (needs.terraform-apply.result == 'success' || needs.terraform-apply.result == 'skipped')
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Run playbook
        run: |
          CMD="ansible-playbook -i ansible/inventory/hosts.yml ansible/playbooks/bootstrap.yml"
          if [ -n "${{ inputs.ansible_tags }}" ]; then
            CMD="$CMD --tags ${{ inputs.ansible_tags }}"
          fi
          if [ "${{ inputs.dry_run }}" = "true" ]; then
            CMD="$CMD --check --diff"
          fi
          $CMD
        env:
          ANSIBLE_FORCE_COLOR: "1"

  argocd-verify:
    name: Verify ArgoCD sync
    runs-on: [self-hosted, homelab]
    needs: [terraform-apply, ansible-run]
    if: |
      always() &&
      !cancelled() &&
      inputs.dry_run == 'false' &&
      (needs.ansible-run.result == 'success' || needs.ansible-run.result == 'skipped') &&
      (needs.terraform-apply.result == 'success' || needs.terraform-apply.result == 'skipped')
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Wait for ArgoCD to sync all apps
        run: |
          export KUBECONFIG="$(pwd)/clusters/homelab/kubeconfig"
          echo "Waiting up to 5 minutes for all ArgoCD apps to sync..."
          timeout 300 bash -c '
            until kubectl -n argocd get applications -o json \
              | jq -e "[.items[] | .status.sync.status] | length > 0 and all(. == \"Synced\")" \
              > /dev/null 2>&1; do
              echo "  still waiting... ($(kubectl -n argocd get applications --no-headers 2>/dev/null | awk "{print \$2}" | sort | uniq -c | tr -s " " | sed "s/^ //"))"
              sleep 15
            done
          '
          echo "All apps synced. Checking health..."
          kubectl -n argocd get applications

      - name: Assert all apps healthy
        run: |
          export KUBECONFIG="$(pwd)/clusters/homelab/kubeconfig"
          UNHEALTHY=$(kubectl -n argocd get applications -o json \
            | jq -r '.items[] | select(.status.health.status != "Healthy") | .metadata.name')
          if [ -n "$UNHEALTHY" ]; then
            echo "Unhealthy apps: $UNHEALTHY"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "All apps are Synced and Healthy."

new='''## Self-hosted runner setup (on the Mac jumpbox)

The runner has to run somewhere with a path into `10.10.10.0/24` and that **survives a cluster rebuild** —
that's the Mac jumpbox (on the Opal LAN, or over the WireGuard tunnel from `bare-metal/README.md`,
"Tunnel WireGuard pour le jumpbox"). Never put it on host1/2/3: they get reset/rebooted during rebuilds.

### Security first (public repo)

This repo is public and the runner holds SSH keys to every node plus a cluster-admin kubeconfig. Two
guards, both required:

1. `plan.yml` jobs only run for pushes and for PRs whose head branch is in this repo
   (`github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`) — fork PRs never reach the
   runner. Keep that `if:` on any new job that targets `[self-hosted, homelab]`.
2. Repo → **Settings → Actions → General → "Approval for running fork pull request workflows"** set to
   **Require approval for all external contributors** (defense in depth for any future workflow).

Also: workflows take inputs via `env:`, never `${{ }}`-interpolated into `run:` scripts.

### Install

1. Get a registration token (single-use, expires after 1h):
   `gh api -X POST repos/maximepatry/k8s-homelab/actions/runners/registration-token -q .token`
   (or repo → **Settings → Actions → Runners → New self-hosted runner**, macOS/ARM64).
2. On the Mac:
   ```bash
   mkdir -p ~/actions-runner && cd ~/actions-runner
   curl -fsSLO https://github.com/actions/runner/releases/download/v<VER>/actions-runner-osx-arm64-<VER>.tar.gz
   tar xzf actions-runner-osx-arm64-<VER>.tar.gz
   ./config.sh --unattended --url https://github.com/maximepatry/k8s-homelab --token <TOKEN> \\
     --name mac-jumpbox --labels homelab --work _work
   ```
   The `homelab` label is required — the workflows target `[self-hosted, homelab]`.
3. Create `~/actions-runner/.env` (read by the runner at start, one `KEY=value` per line, no quotes):
   ```
   PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin
   HOMELAB_TFSTATE=/Users/<you>/projects/k8s-homelab/terraform/cluster-bootstrap/terraform.tfstate
   HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG=/Users/<you>/projects/k8s-homelab/clusters/homelab/kubeconfig
   ```
4. Run it as a launchd service (a LaunchAgent: runs as your user, so it uses your `~/.ssh` keys, and
   only while you're logged in):
   ```bash
   ./svc.sh install && ./svc.sh start
   ./svc.sh status
   ```

Tools the jobs need on that `PATH`: `terraform`, `ansible-playbook` (Homebrew `ansible` bundles
`ansible.posix`/`community.general`), `kubectl`, `jq`.

## State and kubeconfig on the runner

Both live in **your** checkout, not the runner's — the runner's checkout under `~/actions-runner/_work`
is throwaway:

- **Terraform state** is local (`terraform/cluster-bootstrap/terraform.tfstate`, gitignored).
  `backend.tf` declares an explicit `local` backend so CI can run
  `terraform init -backend-config="path=$HOMELAB_TFSTATE"` and share that one file (local-backend locking
  prevents a CI run and a manual `terraform apply` from writing at once). Without it, CI would plan
  against an empty state and try to re-create Cilium/ArgoCD.
- **kubeconfig**: Terraform and `kubectl` read `$HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG` directly. Ansible jobs copy it into
  the checkout first (the control-plane role writes `clusters/homelab/kubeconfig`), and `deploy.yml`
  copies it back if the playbook rewrote it (e.g. after a cluster rebuild).
- Ansible steps run with `working-directory: ansible` so `ansible/ansible.cfg` (become, SSH key, roles
  path) is actually loaded — it's only read from the current directory.
- Plan and Deploy share a `concurrency: homelab-cluster` group, so they never run against the cluster at
  the same time.

The very first run needs an existing cluster and kubeconfig — bootstrap by hand once (see
`docs/ansible.md`, `docs/terraform.md`) before relying on the pipeline.
'''
open(p,'w').write(s[:start]+new)
EOF

- deploy.yml: inputs via env (no shell injection), replace `timeout`
  (absent on macOS) with a deadline loop, sync a rewritten kubeconfig back.
- requirements.yml: pin ansible.posix 2.x and community.general 12.x
  (13.x needs ansible-core >= 2.18; CI uses 2.17).
- docs/ci-cd.md: runner install, .env, security guards.

EOF

input.content:
Prepares the repo for a self-hosted runner on the Mac jumpbox, and pins the Ansible collections. No cluster-facing change: nothing under `clusters/`, `apps/` or the roles changes.

## Security (public repo + self-hosted runner)
- `plan.yml` jobs run only for pushes and same-repo PRs (`head.repo.full_name == github.repository`). A fork PR never reaches the runner, which holds SSH keys to every node and a cluster-admin kubeconfig.
- The plan output reaches `github-script` through `env`, and inputs reach `deploy.yml` through `env`. Nothing is `${{ }}`-interpolated into scripts any more.
- Permissions are least-privilege: `contents: read`, plus `pull-requests: write` only for the plan comment.

## Making the runner jobs actually work
- **Terraform state:** a new `backend.tf` declares an explicit `local` backend, at the same default path as before. CI runs `init -backend-config="path=$HOMELAB_TFSTATE"` to share the operator's state file. Before this, a fresh checkout planned against an empty state, which means re-creating Cilium and ArgoCD. Tested read-only against the live cluster: `0 to add`. The 4 in-place updates are the `---` markers from #2.
- **Kubeconfig:** read from `$HOMELAB_KUBECONFIG`, set in the runner's `.env`. The workspace never had that file.
- **Ansible:** steps run with `working-directory: ansible`, because `ansible.cfg` (become, SSH key) is only read from the current directory.
- **macOS:** `timeout` is replaced by a deadline loop, since macOS doesn't have `timeout`.
- **Concurrency:** Plan and Deploy share a `concurrency: homelab-cluster` group.
- `.github/actionlint.yaml` declares the `homelab` runner label.

## Collections
`ansible.posix` is pinned to `>=2.0.0,<3.0.0` and `community.general` to `>=12.0.0,<13.0.0`. community.general 13.x requires ansible-core >= 2.18, and CI uses 2.17.

## After merge
- Run `terraform init` once in your checkout. The backend block is new, but there's no state migration because it's the same file.
- Register the runner. See `docs/ci-cd.md`.
